items.title: Burkina/Passage de grade : 2 364 policiers en formation pour mieux assumer leurs futures responsabilités
items.description: Burkina-Police-Formation-Passage-Grade Burkina/Passage de grade : 2 364 policiers en formation pour mieux assumer leurs futures responsabilités Ouagadougou, 31 août 2026 (AIB)- Le Directeur général de la Police nationale, Thierry Dofizouho Tuina, a lancé, lundi à Pabré, les formations de passage de grade au titre de l’année 2026, au profit de 2 364 policiers inscrits au tableau d’avancement, afin de renforcer leurs compétences et de les préparer à assumer efficacement les responsabilités liées à leurs futurs grades. Cette formation organisée pour la première fois, concerne 92 commissaires, 304 officiers et 1 968 sous-officiers inscrits au tableau d’avancement, vise à préparer les bénéficiaires à assumer avec compétence et professionnalisme les responsabilités liées à leurs futurs grades. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans la volonté de renforcer les capacités de la Police nationale et de disposer de cadres « patriotiques et compétents » à même de faire face aux défis sécuritaires, a indiqué le Directeur général de la Police nationale, Thierry Dofizouho Tuina. Pour lui, la promotion hiérarchique ne devrait désormais plus reposer sur la seule ancienneté, mais également sur la validation d’un cursus destiné à renforcer les compétences en conception, direction, commandement, planification et gestion opérationnelle. Les formations tirent leur fondement de la loi n°027-2018/AN du 1er juin 2018 portant statut du cadre de la Police nationale, notamment ses articles 107, 109 et 114, ainsi que du décret n°2019-0768/PRES/PM/MSECU/MINEFID relatif aux modalités et critères d’évaluation et d’avancement des personnels de la Police nationale. Le passage de grade tient notamment compte de l’ancienneté, du mérite, du comportement disciplinaire et des formations professionnelles requises. Il est également subordonné aux aptitudes intellectuelles, physiques, morales et professionnelles du policier et concerne les personnels régulièrement inscrits au tableau d’avancement. Au cours de leur formation, les policiers devront notamment maîtriser les nouvelles attributions et limites liées à leurs grades, renforcer leurs compétences professionnelles et techniques, mais aussi actualiser leurs connaissances des lois, règlements et règles déontologiques applicables à la Police nationale. Le Directeur général de la Police a invité les bénéficiaires à suivre assidûment les cours et à considérer les grades auxquels ils aspirent comme des responsabilités et des charges accrues au service de la sécurité des populations. Ces formations dureront deux semaines et se dérouleront à l’Académie de Police, à l’École nationale de Police et dans d’autres centres à l’intérieur du pays. Agence d’information du Burkina YOS/ata

items.title: 2027: Tinubu leads Atiku, Obi in early forecast — PIG
items.description: By Ishola Balogun As Nigeria inches closer to the 2027 presidential election, an early political forecast has placed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu ahead of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi. The Political Intelligence Group (PIG) of Politico.ng, Lagos, in its assessment of the country’s current political configuration, projects that Tinubu would win 20 states if the presidential election were held under the prevailing circumstances. Atiku is projected to win nine states, while Obi is expected to secure eight states, in addition to the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). PIG, however, cautioned that the projection represents a snapshot of the current political landscape and should not be regarded as a prediction of the eventual outcome of the 2027 election. The group noted that Nigeria’s political environment remained fluid and could change significantly before voters go to the polls. “If the election were held today, based on the political realities and alignments currently on the ground, the APC and President Tinubu would have the advantage,” PIG stated in its assessment. “However, this is a projection of the current situation, not a declaration of the eventual result. A lot can happen between now and 2027.” Tinubu projected to win 20 states The forecast gives Tinubu a strong position across the South-West, with the president projected to win all six states in the region. His projected dominance of the zone reflects his longstanding political influence in the South-West, particularly Lagos, where he built much of his political structure before becoming president. Lagos, according to the forecast, remains firmly in Tinubu’s column. The projection also places Kano, one of Nigeria’s most populous states and a major electoral battleground, in the president’s column. A victory in Kano would provide Tinubu with a significant foothold in the North and potentially strengthen his prospects of building a broader national coalition. PIG said the president’s projected advantage extends beyond his traditional South-West base. “Tinubu’s strength, as projected, goes beyond the South-West. His ability to secure states outside his traditional stronghold is an indication of the breadth of the APC’s current political structure,” the group said. The president’s prospects in 2027, however, could depend heavily on how Nigerians assess his administration. Economic hardship, inflation, unemployment, insecurity, infrastructure and the cost of living are expected to feature prominently in the election campaign. PIG identified the economy as potentially the biggest variable in the contest. “The economy remains the biggest variable in this election. If economic conditions improve significantly, it could work in favour of the incumbent. If hardship persists, the opposition will have a powerful campaign issue,” it observed. Atiku projected to win nine states For Atiku, PIG projects victories in nine states, with much of his strength concentrated in the northern part of the country. The former vice president is expected to retain significant support in parts of the North-West and North-East, with Kaduna among the states projected to fall into his column. Atiku’s long political career, extensive political network and experience in presidential contests remain key assets. However, PIG said his major challenge would be converting his northern support into a sufficiently broad national coalition. “Atiku remains a formidable northern political force, but the 2027 contest will require more than regional strength. His ability to make significant inroads into the South will be critical to his prospects,” the group said. The cost of living, particularly the prices of petrol and transportation, could also feature prominently in Atiku’s campaign. The former vice president has criticised aspects of the Federal Government’s economic policies and advocated measures aimed at reducing the burden of fuel prices on Nigerians. PIG noted that if transportation costs and household expenses remain high, the issues could provide the opposition with a potent campaign message. However, any promise of cheaper petrol could also raise questions about how such a policy would be financed and sustained. Obi projected to win eight states, FCT Obi is projected to win eight states, with the FCT also expected to fall into his column. Edo is among the states projected to go to the Labour Party candidate. The forecast reflects the political base Obi built during the 2023 presidential election, when he emerged as a major political force, particularly among younger voters and in several southern states. His political appeal has largely centred on improved economic management, accountability, prudent public spending and more efficient governance. PIG, however, said Obi’s major challenge would be translating that support into a broader geographical coalition capable of delivering victory at the national level. “Obi’s support remains significant, particularly among voters demanding political change and a different style of governance. The question is whether that support can be expanded geographically and translated into sufficient state-by-state victories,” it stated. Obi could also benefit from voter dissatisfaction if economic difficulties persist. However, his prospects could depend heavily on political alliances, party structures and his ability to expand beyond his established areas of strength. Alliances could alter projection PIG identified political realignment as one of the biggest uncertainties surrounding the 2027 election. Opposition parties have continued to explore possible alliances and coalitions aimed at challenging the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). A possible single opposition candidate, defections, choice of running mates, campaign structures and the emergence of new political movements could significantly alter the current electoral calculations. “Alliances, defections, candidates, running mates and the performance of the economy can all alter today’s projection,” PIG noted. Religion, ethnicity and regional identity are also expected to influence political calculations, particularly in the choice of presidential and vice-presidential candidates. However, the group said these traditional factors would compete with bread-and-butter issues such as security, jobs, inflation, food prices, petrol prices and the general standard of living. ‘Snapshot, not verdict’ The projected figures — Tinubu 20 states, Atiku nine and Obi eight — add up to 37 states, excluding the FCT, which is projected to Obi. PIG stressed that the figures should not be mistaken for an election result, describing the assessment as a reflection of the current balance of political forces. “Our projection should be understood as a political snapshot. It reflects the balance of forces as they currently exist. It does not mean the election has already been won or lost,” the group said. The political landscape is expected to evolve as the major parties consolidate their structures, potential presidential candidates intensify consultations and opposition forces decide whether to contest independently or form alliances. For Tinubu, the immediate challenge will be to convert incumbency, party structure and projected regional strength into sustained national support. For Atiku, the task will be to preserve his northern base while expanding his reach into other regions. For Obi, the challenge will be to transform the momentum of 2023 into a broader national coalition. For now, however, the PIG forecast places Tinubu ahead with 20 states, followed by Atiku with nine and Obi with eight, while the FCT is projected to Obi. With the 2027 presidential election still ahead, the political map remains subject to significant change. items.title: Peace march in AJK's Sudhnoti demands early elections, end to blockades
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: A large number of people from different walks of life took part in a peace march on Monday in Palandri, the district headquarters of Sudhnoti in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), calling for an end to unrest and blockades and immediate elections in seven constituencies of Poonch and Sudhnoti. Recent elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were held in phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10. Organised by the Public Alliance Forum Sudhnoti, the march began at Kotli Chowk and passed through various streets before culminating in a public gathering at Kutchery Chowk. The participants carried AJK and Pakistani flags, with banners bearing slogans such as “This homeland is ours, we are its guardians”, “Unrest in the state is unacceptable”, “Lawlessness in the state is unacceptable” and “What do we want? Peace!” Representatives of the PML-N, PPP, Muslim Conference, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam, Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Party, Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party and PTI, alongside traders, lawyers, transporters, civil society representatives, educationists and ex-servicemen, addressed the gathering. In a joint declaration, the participants urged the governments of Pakistan and AJK to immediately hold elections in the seven constituencies of Poonch and Sudhnoti where polling could not take place during the recent AJK elections due to the law and order situation. They also called for the immediate removal of blockades by both the government and protesters, whether inside AJK or at entry points into Pakistan, to ease the public’s difficulties in travelling and obtaining essential goods. The participants additionally demanded the restoration of travel and educational facilities, particularly in Sudhnoti and Poonch; the immediate restoration of internet services across AJK; and uninterrupted supplies of food and other essential commodities from Pakistan. They said restrictions on the movement of these goods had compounded the difficulties faced by the people. It also called for adequate supplies of wheat to flour mills to ensure the regular distribution of flour, uninterrupted availability of petrol and hassle-free processing of documents required by people travelling abroad. Participants also expressed concern over rumours of the possible relocation of educational and administrative institutions from Rawalakot. They demanded that the “endless sacrifices” made by the “brave, courageous and patriotic people” of the region for the Kashmir freedom movement and the “completion of Pakistan” should not be overlooked, urging the authorities to avoid any such step. It reiterated that no one could weaken the “everlasting bond” between Kashmiris and Pakistan and that a strong and stable Pakistan was the guarantor of the freedom movement, while AJK served as a “strong defence shield” for Pakistan. “Promoting instability in the region will not be allowed,” the participants declared. The peace march also congratulated the government of Pakistan and the armed forces for what it described as their role in promoting global peace. The PML-N’s Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani was elected as AJK PM after being sworn in last Friday. His sole contender was PPP’s Sardar Mukhtar Ahmed Abbasi, who bagged 14 votes in the contest for the top office. The third phase of polling was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. The AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation. In the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party also joined hands with the PML-N . As for the reserved seats, the PML-N bagged six and the PPP two. The PPP alleged widespread rigging and irregularities in the elections.

items.title: Abu Jinapor highlights increased gold exports after Domestic Gold Purchase Programme
items.description: Former Lands and Natural Resources Minister Samuel Abdulai Jinapor has highlighted Ghana’s significant gold export earnings in 2024 as evidence of the impact of policies introduced under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. Mr Jinapor, who is now the Member of Parliament for Damongo, said the government introduced a series of measures to strengthen the programme and ensure that gold produced by licensed operators contributed directly to Ghana’s reserves and foreign exchange position. He said the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources engaged the Ghana Chamber of Mines and the Ghana National Association of Small Scale Miners before invoking the government’s pre-emptory right under Section 7 of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703). According to him, directives issued in November 2023 required large-scale mining companies to sell 20 per cent of their refined gold to the Bank of Ghana in Ghana cedis before exporting the remainder. He said Community Mining Schemes and licensed small-scale miners were also required to sell their gold to the government through the then Precious Minerals Marketing Company (PMMC), with the relevant licences containing clauses to that effect. Mr Jinapor said the measures were deliberately focused on licensed and responsible small-scale miners because the government did not want illegally sourced gold to enter the programme. He said the Minerals Commission, PMMC and Bank of Ghana coordinated and enforced the directives with support from the Ghana Chamber of Mines and the Ghana National Association of Small Scale Miners. He also noted that the government subsequently directed the Minerals Commission and PMMC not to process gold export licence applications without the express written approval of the Minister. The measures, Mr Jinapor said, resulted in Ghana’s gold exports reaching US$11.6 billion in 2024, compared with US$7.6 billion in 2023 and US$6.6 billion in 2022. He argued that the figures demonstrated the importance of the gold sector to Ghana’s economy and the effectiveness of measures introduced to strengthen domestic gold purchasing and reserve accumulation. The Damongo MP also maintained that the reserves accumulated through the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme had become an important pillar of Ghana’s economy. Citing Bank of Ghana Governor Dr Johnson Asiama, Mr Jinapor said the programme had “strengthened external buffers and macroeconomic stability” and had been “crucial to the stabilisation goal of the Bank of Ghana.” He concluded that the public record should recognise Dr Mahamudu Bawumia as the originator of the programme.

items.title: 2027: We have words, courts, laws as weapons — ADC
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress, ADC, on Monday vowed to resist alleged intimidation and attempts to frustrate its candidates ahead of the 2027 general election, declaring that it would deploy the courts, laws and its voice rather than violence. With campaigns gathering momentum, the opposition party said its candidates must be prepared to confront provocations through lawful means while keeping their own campaigns free of hate speech, ethnic and religious profiling and political violence. Briefing journalists after a consultation meeting with the party’s governorship candidates from across the country in Abuja, ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said the meeting was convened not only to prepare the candidates for the general election but also to address divisions arising from the party’s primaries. Responding to concerns that ADC candidates could face attacks on their campaign trains, destruction of billboards or attempts to stop them from campaigning in some states, Abdullahi said the party would not retaliate with violence, insisting that it would resist such moves through lawful means. “We have words that we will use as weapons. We have courts that we use as weapons. We have laws that we use as weapons, and we will fight it because we are democrats,” he said. Reconciliation committee coming Abdullahi said the party would soon constitute a National Reconciliation Committee to resolve post-primary grievances and rebuild relationships among members ahead of the general election. He urged the governorship candidates to close ranks with those who contested against them during the primaries, stressing that the party needed to go into the election as a united force. ADC puts subsidy at heart of campaign Beyond reconciliation, Abdullahi said the meeting also focused on the party’s national campaign agenda, particularly its promise to restore fuel subsidy as part of measures to reduce the cost of living. He said the candidates had been directed to make the issue a major plank of their campaigns, adding that the party would provide them with details of how it intended to implement the policy. According to him, the proposal was one of the issues expected to distinguish ADC from other political parties and form a central part of its message to voters. ’We won’t answer violence with violence’ But while urging its candidates to take the party’s message to voters, Abdullahi acknowledged that they could face resistance in some states, including attacks on campaign trains, destruction of billboards and attempts to prevent them from campaigning. He said the party was no stranger to adversity, but insisted that such provocations would not push ADC into retaliation. “Violence is not the ADC way. Whenever we are confronted with any form of provocation, we will resist it and we will challenge it within legal means,” he said. The party, he added, was also compiling alleged cases of what it described as ‘political terrorism’ involving members of the ruling party, including reported threats against voters who refused to support the APC. “We are compiling the list of this kind of cases, and we are going to make it open. We are going to challenge them,” he stated. Abdullahi also alleged that exorbitant charges imposed for opposition billboards in some states were aimed at shutting the party out of the communication space. He said ADC would resist such restrictions through the courts and existing laws, rather than allow itself to be pushed into confrontation. ADC warns own candidates While drawing a line between lawful resistance and political violence, Abdullahi said the party’s rules would apply equally to its own candidates. He said ADC would not shield any candidate found violating its prohibition against political violence or other forms of misconduct, stressing that the party was being built with the capacity to enforce discipline among its members. “What we have emphasised from the start is that we are building a party that is able to impose its authority on its own candidates,” he said. No substitution complaint, party says On reports of possible substitution of validly nominated candidates by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Abdullahi said no candidate had complained to the party about being replaced. He said ADC had records of the candidates submitted to INEC, while the electoral commission also had acknowledgements of the submissions. “If at any point it’s brought to our notice that any candidate is swapped, we will deal with it administratively,” he said. Mark warns against hate speech Earlier at the meeting, National Chairman of the party, Senator David Mark, charged the governorship candidates to run issue-based campaigns and avoid empty promises, warning that pledges made without the intention to fulfil them could damage the integrity of the party. Mark also urged the candidates to familiarise themselves with the ADC’s Governance and Ethical Principles contained in its ‘Orange Book’, as well as the party’s manifesto. “We are ADC. Our campaign must reflect the kind of country that we would like to build. Avoid hate speech, ethnic or religious profiling. We cannot be associated with violence in whatever form,” he said. The candidates expressed appreciation to the party for giving them the platform to contest the 2027 election and pledged their loyalty, promising to make the party proud by winning their respective elections. items.title: Moyen-Orient : Reprise des bombardements entre les USA et l’Iran
items.description: Les États-Unis ont mené, dans la nuit du dimanche 30 au lundi 31 août 2026, de nouvelles frappes contre la République islamique d’Iran, visant cette fois l’île de Larak, dans le détroit d’Ormuz. Il s’agit des premiers bombardements américains depuis un mois. L’attaque a fait deux morts, selon l’agence de presse iranienne Tasnim. Téhéran a immédiatement riposté en ciblant des positions américaines en Jordanie. Selon un commandement militaire américain, les frappes ont été ordonnées par le président Donald Trump après que des forces des Gardiens de la Révolution islamique ont été repérées en train de préparer des roquettes chargées de mines marines, prêtes à être lancées dans le détroit d’Ormuz, voie stratégique pour le transport pétrolier. Dans un message officiel, le président Trump a également affirmé que l’île de Kharg, important terminal énergétique iranien, avait été « réduite en miettes ». Cette déclaration a toutefois été démentie plus tard par un responsable américain, qui a précisé que cette île n’avait pas été visée par les raids. Ces frappes n’ont pas laissé Téhéran indifférent. Les Gardiens de la Révolution, après avoir promis des « représailles », ont annoncé avoir attaqué, à l’aide de missiles balistiques et de drones, deux bases aériennes abritant des troupes américaines en Jordanie. « Tout acte d’hostilité se heurtera à des représailles encore plus puissantes », ont-ils prévenu, dans des propos relayés par les médias d’État iraniens. Ces affrontements surviennent après deux mois de cessez-le-feu entre Washington et Téhéran concernant le détroit d’Ormuz, relançant les craintes d’une escalade régionale. Minute.bf

items.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs0.77, cuts high-speed diesel price by Rs1.03
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Monday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.77 per litre and cut that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.03 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs342.79 per litre while HSD will cost Rs370.41 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on September 1 (Tuesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: EFCC sacks over 40 staff for corruption, prosecutes 5 others
items.description: The Chairman, Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Mr Ola Olukoyede, says more than 40 staff members have been dismissed for corruption and financial malpractice in the last three years. Olukoyede disclosed this on Monday in Abuja at a media interactive session to mark his three-year stewardship at the commission’s headquarters. The chairman also said that about five of the commission’s staff are currently being prosecuted for corrupt practices. “In the past two and a half to three years of my service, I have asked them to dismiss over 40 staff on account of corruption and financial malpractice. More than five of them are being prosecuted at the moment,” he said. The EFCC chairman said some of the affected staff members are already being prosecuted, while case files involving others are being prepared for prosecution. “You can follow those cases in court; they are public knowledge. “If that is what people do in other agencies and I arrest them, I investigate them, I prosecute them, why must I just dismiss you if you do it within our own system and I’m not prosecuting you?” he asked. Olukoyede said the disciplinary measures were part of efforts to ensure EFCC personnel were held to the same standards of accountability the agency demanded from other Nigerians. “You must be sure that your hands are clean. You can’t be fighting corruption when your hands are soiled with corrupt practices,” he said. The EFCC chairman also announced the renaming of the commission’s former Internal Affairs Department to the Department of Ethics and Integrity as part of its drive for “internal cleansing.” He said the commission had also introduced a gift policy to strengthen transparency and prevent conflicts of interest. According to him, under the policy, staff will be required to declare gifts above a specified value, including those received from friends and relatives at home and abroad. “The commission will also define the categories of gifts personnel can accept and require officers to account for their sources of income and standard of living,” he added. The chairman called for stronger institutional reforms and policy changes to fight corruption, saying law enforcement alone could not win the war. “The most effective system that fights financial crime is not law enforcement. It is the policy regime, institutional reforms that close leakages,” he said. He urged the media and civil society to return to their watchdog roles. (NAN) The post EFCC sacks over 40 staff for corruption, prosecutes 5 others appeared first on Vanguard News .

EFL blasts UEFA over Champions League, League Cup fixture clash
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The English Football League (EFL) has expressed disappointment with UEFA after the European football governing body scheduled a Champions League fixture involving Liverpool on the same night as Everton’s Carabao Cup clash with Wolverhampton Wanderers. According to Reuters, the EFL said UEFA’s decision forced it to rearrange fixtures after Liverpool’s Champions League meeting with Atletico Madrid was scheduled for September 9, the same date initially fixed for Everton’s home tie against Wolves. The EFL said logistical challenges involving the police meant Liverpool and Everton could not host home matches on the same evening. “On 28 August we confirmed that the Carabao Cup Round Three tie between Everton and Wolverhampton Wanderers had been scheduled for Wednesday 9 September,” the EFL said in a statement. The league said the fixture had been confirmed with local stakeholders before UEFA announced Liverpool’s Champions League game for the same date. “On Saturday, UEFA announced that it had scheduled Liverpool v Atletico Madrid for the same date, despite it being clear that Everton and Liverpool cannot play home fixtures on the same evening,” the EFL added. The EFL said it met UEFA officials on Monday to explore alternative arrangements but claimed the European body was unwilling to move the Liverpool fixture because of the impact on overseas supporters. As a result, Everton’s meeting with Wolves has been moved to September 16. Liverpool’s League Cup fixture against Tottenham Hotspur, which had been scheduled for September 16, has now been brought forward by 24 hours. The EFL criticised UEFA’s handling of the situation, saying domestic leagues had repeatedly made adjustments to accommodate the expansion of UEFA club competitions. “Over recent seasons the League has made a number of changes to accommodate the expansion of UEFA Club competitions — a decision which was made without adequate consultation with domestic leagues,” the EFL said. “This makes UEFA’s unwillingness to cooperate all the more frustrating, not least for the supporters of the five impacted clubs, and we sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused.” UEFA had not responded to the EFL’s criticism at the time of the report. The fixture changes affect supporters of Everton, Wolves, Liverpool, Tottenham and Atletico Madrid. The post EFL blasts UEFA over Champions League, League Cup fixture clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: BURKINA-RETROUVAILLES-COLLEGE-TENKODOGO Boulgou/Tenkodogo : La promotion 1983-1987 du collège Marie Reine renoue avec son établissement Tenkodogo, 29 août 2026 (AIB) – La promotion 1983-1987 du collège Marie Reine de Tenkodogo a effectué samedi un retour aux sources, marqué par des retrouvailles avec ses anciens enseignants, une prière d'action de grâce et la remise d'une tonne de ciment au profit de l'initiative présidentielle Faso Mêbo. Plus de quatre décennies après leur passage au collège, les anciennes élèves ont renoué avec leur établissement dans une ambiance de souvenir et de fraternité. Pour l'ancien professeur Benjamin Zoungrana, cette rencontre est empreinte d'une émotion particulière. « C'est une joie immense de les revoir. Je les ai connues jeunes filles, les retrouver femmes aujourd'hui me procure une grande satisfaction », a-t-il confié. M. Zoungrana a souhaité que ce premier noyau s'élargisse à l'ensemble de la promotion. Il a eu une pensée pieuse pour les élèves et enseignants décédés, avant d'exhorter la jeunesse à plus d'écoute envers les parents et les éducateurs, ainsi qu’à un usage responsable des outils numériques au service des études. Au-delà des retrouvailles, la démarche se veut citoyenne, a indiqué Clarisse Minoungou/Bancé, porte-parole de la promotion. Selon les explications données après la prière d'action de grâce, les anciennes élèves ont voulu répondre à l'appel du Chef de l'Etat, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, concernant la mobilisation pour la construction nationale. « Ce geste représente notre modeste contribution à la construction de la patrie », a précisé Mme Minoungou/Bancé. La promotion a ainsi remis une tonne de ciment destinée à l'initiative Faso Mêbo. Elle a, à cette occasion, invité les autres promotions du collège Marie Reine à emboîter le pas. Par cet acte, la promotion 1983-1987 a allié devoir de mémoire, de reconnaissance et d’engagement citoyen. Agence d'Information du Burkina SM/ata/zs

items.title: Everton bid for US striker Balogun after World Cup controversy
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Everton have stepped up their pursuit of United States striker Folarin Balogun, submitting a bid for the Monaco forward as they look to strengthen their attack before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. According to BBC Sport, Everton have made an offer for the 25-year-old, who is valued at £40m by Monaco, with the former Arsenal striker emerging as a key target for the Premier League club. ESPN, however, reports that Everton have submitted a £35m offer for Balogun, worth about $47.5m, with the club closing in on a possible deal for the United States international. Balogun’s potential return to the Premier League comes only weeks after he was at the centre of one of the biggest controversies of the 2026 World Cup. The US striker scored three goals during the tournament but was sent off for serious foul play in the last-32 clash against Bosnia-Herzegovina. Although he was expected to serve an automatic suspension, FIFA’s disciplinary committee suspended the ban for a year, allowing Balogun to feature in the United States’ last-16 defeat by Belgium. The decision sparked widespread criticism, particularly after reports emerged that US President Donald Trump and White House officials had lobbied FIFA over the American striker’s punishment. UEFA described the decision to allow Balogun to play as “unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable”, while FIFA president Gianni Infantino denied influencing disciplinary decisions. Balogun had earlier attracted attention at the World Cup with his goalscoring form for the US, having chosen to represent the country despite being eligible to play for England and Nigeria. ESPN described his tournament as a major success before the red-card controversy, while Sky Sports highlighted his three World Cup goals as part of the reasons behind Everton’s interest. The forward joined Monaco from Arsenal in 2023 and has scored 31 goals in 91 appearances for the French club, according to Sky Sports. Everton are looking to add another forward after Beto moved closer to a transfer to Fiorentina. ESPN reports that the Portuguese striker is set to join the Serie A club for a fee in the region of £15m. Everton had also been considering a move for Tottenham striker Richarlison, but Sky Sports reported that the club’s focus had been on bringing their former forward back to Goodison Park, with Balogun another option. However, with the transfer deadline approaching, Everton have now made their move for Balogun. A return to England would give the US striker another opportunity to establish himself in the Premier League after leaving Arsenal for Monaco three years ago. Sky Sports reported that Balogun finished last season strongly for Monaco, scoring 11 goals in his final 14 matches, including a Champions League brace against Paris Saint-Germain. Everton will now wait to see whether their offer is enough to convince Monaco to part with the World Cup scorer before the transfer window closes. The post Everton bid for US striker Balogun after World Cup controversy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sissili/Léo : L’association « Dabari Ywani » promeut le développement local et la cohésion sociale lors de ses 72 heures
items.description: BURKINA-PROMOTION-DEVELOPPEMENT-LOCAL-COMMUNE-LEO Sissili/Léo : L’association « Dabari Ywani » promeut le développement local et la cohésion sociale lors de ses 72 heures Léo, 30 août 2026 (AIB) – L’association « Dabari Ywani » a célébré, du 28 au 30 août 2026 à Léo, la 5ᵉ édition de ses « 72 heures » sous le thème : « Bâtir le développement local dans la cohésion sociale et la paix ». Placé sous la présidence du Haut-commissaire de la province de la Sissili, Téwindé Isaac Sia, et le parrainage de l’entrepreneur et chef Dozo, Eidel Moussa Nébié dit Papa Tchèfari, cet événement a allié promotion culturelle, assainissement, reboisement et sport. Née d’une amitié d’enfance concrétisée en structure associative il y a cinq ans, l’association Dabari Ywani entend apporter sa pierre à l’épanouissement de la province. Selon son président du conseil d’administration, Moussa Nignan, ce rendez-vous annuel constitue un cadre d’action concrète pour la collectivité. « À la base, c’est une affaire de quartier, une amitié d’enfance qui s’est traduite en association il y a 5 ans de cela. L’objectif est d’apporter notre pierre, comme on peut, au développement de notre localité qui nous est chère : la Sissili en particulier et le Burkina Faso en général », a-t-il expliqué. Au programme de cette édition, une visite guidée du musée Tikéli de Léo pour magnifier le patrimoine culturel local, une plantation d’arbres sur le site muséal afin d’ombrager le cadre ainsi qu’une action sociale en faveur de la santé publique. Un lot de matériel d’hygiène et d’assainissement a été remis symboliquement au district sanitaire pour équiper le Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) de Léo et les CSPS environnants. Réceptionnant l’équipement, le représentant du Médecin-chef du district (MCD), Séni Ouétian, a exprimé sa gratitude. « Ce matériel va nous aider au niveau de notre centre de santé. Cela va améliorer l’hygiène dans nos salles de consultation et offrir à nos patients un environnement plus confortable », a-t-il affirmé, invitant les bénéficiaires à un usage responsable des bacs à ordures mis à leur disposition. Présidant la cérémonie, le Haut-commissaire de la Sissili, Téwindé Isaac Sia, a salué la maturité de la jeunesse et réaffirmé l’accompagnement de l’État. « Comme vous le savez, l’État, à lui seul, ne peut pas tout faire. Il va falloir que les structures associatives arrivent à l’accompagner et à mener des activités entrant dans le cadre du développement, de la cohésion sociale et du vivre-ensemble », a souligné l’autorité provinciale. Camarade Sia a également félicité le responsable du musée Tikéli pour sa clairvoyance qui favorise le positionnement de la province comme un pôle touristique majeur. Les activités se sont achevées ce dimanche 30 août sur une note sportive avec le match de football U15 opposant Relève FC à Avenir FC, deux équipes issues du centre de formation du coach Aboudé. Relève FC s’est imposée sur le score de 1 but à 0, s’adjugeant le trophée assorti d’une enveloppe financière de dix mille francs. Agence d’Information du Burkina BAN/ata/zs

items.title: Arsenal face Villa test as Konsa set for emotional return
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Arsenal will look to continue their perfect start to the Premier League season when they visit Aston Villa at Villa Park on Monday night, with the champions facing a side desperate to recover from a humiliating opening-day defeat. The match, according to Sky Sports, is scheduled for 8pm at Villa Park, with Arsenal arriving after a 3-0 victory over newly promoted Coventry City, while Villa were thrashed 4-0 by Brighton in their opening league game. Mikel Arteta’s side are bidding to maintain their 100 per cent start and extend their impressive record in opening away matches. Arsenal have won their first away league game in each of the last four seasons, keeping clean sheets in all four, although they have never made it five successive campaigns. Villa, meanwhile, face a major test after a turbulent summer that saw several key members of their Europa League-winning squad leave the club. Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea for £117m, Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United, Lucas Digne joined Paris Saint-Germain, while striker Ollie Watkins completed a move to Al Hilal. Arsenal also signed centre-back Ezri Konsa from Villa in a deal reported by Sky Sports to be worth around £55m. Konsa could make his Arsenal debut against his former employers, adding an intriguing subplot to the encounter. The defender did not feature in Arsenal’s opening league victory, but Arteta has indicated that he could be ready to play at Villa Park. Sky Sports reports that the move represents a significant change in Arsenal’s transfer strategy, despite the club already having several options in defence. For Villa manager Unai Emery, the challenge is immediate. His side conceded four goals before half-time against Brighton, with Joao Gomes also sent off in a disastrous opening 45 minutes. Sky Sports noted that Villa became only the second side in Premier League history to concede four goals, receive a red card and score an own goal in the first half. The loss of Konsa has also been highlighted as one of Villa’s biggest problems. Their defensive frailties were exposed repeatedly against Brighton, with individual errors contributing to the heavy defeat. Villa will be without Gomes through suspension, while Amadou Onana is expected to miss the season with an ACL injury. New arrivals Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki, Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Leon Goretzka could also be in contention to make their Villa debuts. Arsenal, meanwhile, could welcome Bruno Guimaraes back into Premier League action after a groin problem, while Jurrien Timber is nearing a return. William Saliba remains unavailable with a long-term back injury. The Gunners also have a strong historical record at Villa Park, having won 15 Premier League matches at the venue — more than at any other away ground in the competition. However, Villa won the most recent meeting at the stadium, securing a dramatic 2-1 victory last season through a stoppage-time Emiliano Buendia goal. Arsenal responded by winning the return fixture 4-1 at the Emirates. The fixture therefore presents contrasting challenges for both sides: Arsenal are seeking another statement win in their title defence, while Villa need an immediate response to their opening-day collapse. Arteta has also backed Emery to turn Villa’s fortunes around, describing his compatriot as one of the Premier League’s most experienced and successful managers. “He is one of the most experienced managers in the league, and one of the most successful without a shadow of a doubt,” Arteta said. “What Villa did last year and how they finished, it was an incredible season. It’s just one game and that’s it – I’m sure he will turn it around.” With Arsenal aiming to maintain their perfect start and Villa seeking redemption, all eyes will be on Villa Park when the two sides meet tonight. items.title: Karim Benzema leaves Al Hilal after less than eight months at Saudi Club
items.description: Former France and Real Madrid striker Karim Benzema has left Al Hilal just under eight months after joining the Saudi club. “Al Hilal Club Company and French player Karim Benzema have mutually agreed to terminate their contractual relationship, bringing his time with Al Hilal’s first football team to an end,” wrote the club on their website on Monday. “Al Hilal Club Company expressed its appreciation for Benzema’s contributions during his time with the team, as well as the professionalism, commitment, and leadership he demonstrated both on and off the pitch,” said the statement. Benzema thanked the club on social media. “A chapter comes to an end,” he posted. The former Ballon d’Or winner moved to Saudi Arabia from Real Madrid in 2023, joining Al Ittihad and leading the Jeddah club to a Saudi Pro League title in 2025. After a dispute over a contract extension in late January he moved to Al Hilal in Riyadh for the rest of the season. He had one year left on his contract, but has a deal until 2030 as an “ambassador” for Saudi tourism and the 2034 World Cup. The announcement that the 38-year-old was leaving came the day after Al Hilal signed 30-year-old England centre forward Ollie Watkins from Aston Villa for a reported £50 million ($68 million). Spanish sports daily AS reported that Benzema had no intention of retiring and had offers from the American MLS and other Saudi clubs. Al Hilal wished Benzema “every success in the next chapter of his career”. items.title: Boulgou/Tenkodogo : Les commerçants plantent 110 arbres pour protéger un site coutumier
items.description: BURKINA-REBOISEMENT-SITE-COUTUME Boulgou/Tenkodogo : Les commerçants plantent 110 arbres pour protéger un site coutumier Tenkodogo, 29 août 2026 (AIB) – L'Union des commerçants et assimilés de Tenkodogo (UCAT) a organisé, samedi 29 août 2026, la troisième édition de sa journée de reboisement, consacrée à la sécurisation d'un site de rites coutumiers. Environ 110 plants ont été mis en terre et sécurisés sur le lieu. L'activité, placée sous la présidence du Haut-commissaire de la province du Boulgou, Constantin Dabiré, s'est déroulée en présence de responsables coutumiers, de représentants du secteur culturel et des parrains. Pour les organisateurs, cette action vise à contribuer à la restauration de l'environnement, tout en participant à la préservation du patrimoine culturel et coutumier. Le Haut-commissaire du Boulgou a salué une initiative qui allie reboisement et sauvegarde des espaces sacrés. « Chaque association sérieuse doit inscrire ce genre d'initiatives dans son programme d'activités pour contribuer au développement », a déclaré M. Dabiré, invitant les autres associations à s'inspirer de l'exemple de l'UCAT. Il a exhorté les participants à poursuivre le reboisement à domicile et à assurer l'entretien et la protection des plants mis en terre. Le représentant de la direction régionale en charge de la Culture, El Hadj Abdoul Kabiro Sana, par ailleurs président de l'UCAT, a souligné l'importance de la protection des sites coutumiers, qui permet de sauvegarder les traditions et les rites qui y sont pratiqués. Il a annoncé que les services compétents entendent documenter ces sites en vue de leur préservation, de leur sécurisation et de leur éventuelle inscription au patrimoine national. Le Secrétaire général du Patronat du Nakambé, Emmanuel Sorgho, représentant le parrain Seydou Sawadogo, vice-président du Patronat burkinabè des commerçants, a félicité l'UCAT pour cette initiative et a assuré que le Patronat accompagnera les actions de sécurisation des sites coutumiers, y compris lors des prochaines éditions. Au nom de Sa Majesté Naaba Guiguempolé, Dima de Zoungrantenga, Roi de Tenkodogo, Saanaba Sigri a exprimé la reconnaissance de la chefferie coutumière. « L'eau, c'est la vie, l'arbre aussi c'est la vie », a-t-il déclaré, rappelant les multiples vertus de l'arbre. Il a précisé que le site concerné sert d'aire de battage du mil et constitue également un lieu de rites coutumiers. Il a encouragé les commerçants à poursuivre leurs actions et invité les autres associations à emboîter le pas pour contribuer à la sécurisation des différents sites coutumiers. Cette troisième édition a ainsi mis en lumière le lien entre protection de l'environnement et sauvegarde du patrimoine coutumier. Les responsables présents ont appelé à la pérennisation de l'initiative et à l'entretien des 110 plants mis en terre. Agence d'Information du Burkina SM/ata/zs

items.title: Access Bank Guinée célèbre cinq années d’engagement en faveur du progrès et de la création d’opportunités.
items.description: Conakry, Guinée: Access Bank Guin ée célèbre son cinquième anniversaire, marquant cinq années au service de ses clients, de soutien aux entreprises et de contribution au développement économique de la Guinée à travers la croissance, l’innovation et un impact porteur de sens. En tant que membre d’Access Bank Group e , l’une des principales institutions financières d’Afrique, au service de plus de 60 millions de clients dans 25 marchés à travers le monde, Access Bank Guinée élargi l’accès aux services financiers, soutenu des secteurs clés de l’économie et aidé les particuliers et les entreprises à saisir des opportunités de croissance. Depuis le début de ses activités, la Banque a accordé près de 500 milliards GNF de financements pour soutenir l’activité économique dans des secteurs stratégiques, notamment les mines, l’énergie, les télécommunications, le commerce, le ciment et la construction. Au cours de la même période, le total des actifs a atteint 1 979 milliards GNF, tandis que la Banque a établi des relations de confiance avec plus de 13 000 clients et plus de 15 grandes entreprises. Access Bank Guin ée a également fait progresser la banque digitale et l’inclusion financière grâce à des solutions telles qu’ Access More , USSD Banking, Primus Plus et Bank to Wallet, ainsi qu’à travers son intégration aux plateformes nationales, notamment e-Tax, GUCEG et le Switch National. Ces solutions ont contribué à rendre les services bancaires plus simples, plus accessibles et plus pratiques pour les clients à travers le pays. L’engagement de la Banque en faveur de l’innovation et de l’expérience client lui a valu la distinction de Most Innovative Digital Bank 2025, tandis que la solidité de ses fondamentaux commerciaux a favorisé un retour à la rentabilité et une croissance soutenue. Au-delà de ses activités bancaires, Access Bank Guin ée a, au cours de ces cinq dernières années, renforcé son engagement auprès des communautés à travers des initiatives à fort impact social. La Banque a notamment fait don d’équipements médicaux au Centre de Santé de Matam, déployé sa campagne Octobre Rose dans 19 structures hospitalières, accompagné des PME à travers des programmes de formation et d’inclusion financière, offert des livres aux élèves de l’École primaire SIG Madina et apporté son soutien à un orphelinat. Ces actions témoignent de la volonté d’Access Bank Guin ée de contribuer durablement au bien-être des populations et au développement socio-économique de la Guinée. S’exprimant à l’occasion de cette étape importante, Jean Louis Haba, Directeur Général d’Access Bank Guin ée , a déclaré : « Il y a cinq ans, nous avons commencé notre aventure en Guinée avec l’engagement d’être plus qu’une banque. Alors que nous nous tournons vers l’avenir, nous restons déterminés à stimuler l’innovation, soutenir les entreprises, autonomiser les communautés et créer une valeur durable pour la Guinée. » Alors qu’elle entame son prochain chapitre, Access Bank Guin ée restera concentrée sur l’approfondissement de l’inclusion financière, le soutien au commerce et à l’entrepreneuriat, l’accélération de l’innovation digitale et la création d’un impact durable, conformément à la vision d’Access Bank Group e de devenir la banque africaine la plus respectée au monde. NPP UK branch calls for independent audit into gold purchasing operations and parliamentary probe
items.description: The UK branch of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) has issued a formal statement urging full transparency, institutional accountability, and a thorough independent forensic audit into Ghana’s domestic gold purchasing transactions. The statement follows the Speaker of Parliament’s decision to admit a Minority motion for a public inquiry into the matter. While welcoming the parliamentary inquiry, the NPP UK Branch emphasised that any probe must be grounded in an objective financial evaluation. “For the enquiry to command public trust and deliver credible outcomes, it must be informed by an independent forensic audit,” the statement signed by NPP UK Branch Chairman Andy Owusu read. “The audit should be conducted by reputable, non-partisan experts to focus the inquest, establish the facts, and ensure the process is not politicised.” Clarifying the Financial Assessment The call for scrutiny centres on disclosures referenced in a recent International Monetary Fund (IMF) report regarding financial adjustments under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP). While political debate has surrounded the figures, macro-level economic analyses clarify that the cited $1.7 billion assessment reflects policy, exchange-rate, and valuation costs incurred directly by the Bank of Ghana (BoG) to build national reserves, rather than commercial trading losses incurred by Ghana GoldBOD. Nonetheless, the NPP UK Branch stressed that the overall magnitude of the figures—representing a significant national financial footprint—requires complete clarity . “A loss of this magnitude by a single public entity raises fundamental questions about economic stewardship, institutional oversight, and the competence of the current administration,” the statement noted . “The full nature and character of GoldBOD’s transactions must therefore be subjected to rigorous public scrutiny.” Distractions and Demands for Governance Standards The diaspora branch also addressed the escalating public friction between officials, taking exception to allegations made by GoldBOD Chief Executive Officer, Mr Sammy Gyamfi, against Minority Leader Hon. Alexander Afenyo-Markin. “Under Ghanaian law, extortion is a criminal offence and must be proven with evidence,” the release stated. “In the absence of proof, such claims risk being viewed as a calculated and desperate attempt to shield what may be the gravest financial inquiry in our recent history.” The group expressed its full solidarity with Hon. Afenyo-Markin for his defence of public interest. To ensure thorough public accountability, the NPP UK Branch outlined three primary demands : Independent Forensic Audit: A comprehensive audit of all gold purchase transactions over the last 18 months conducted by a non-partisan body to serve as the foundation for Parliament’s inquiry. Institutional Investigation: An immediate review by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) into GoldBOD’s operational activities. Non-Partisan Oversight: Demonstrated impartiality from Operation Recover All Loots (ORAL) to assure the public that accountability remains free of political favour. Concluding the statement, the leadership reiterated that the ongoing controversy reflects broader concerns regarding fiscal management and public trust. “Ghana deserves better. Ghana demands transparency, discipline, and respect for public funds,” Mr Owusu affirmed.

items.title: Gnagna/Bogandé : autorités, populations et orpailleurs mobilisés pour une communauté en bonne santé
items.description: BURKINA-GNAGNA-SANTE-MOBILISATION Gnagna/Bogandé : autorités, populations et orpailleurs mobilisés pour une communauté en bonne santé Bogandé, 29 août 2026 (AIB) – Une forte mobilisation des autorités administratives, des populations, des acteurs de la santé et de l’Association Boalihammou des orpailleurs de la Sirba a marqué, samedi à Bogandé, le lancement officiel de la première édition de la Semaine d’activités socio-sanitaires de l’Association Baani-Mani Santé pour Tous, placée sous le thème : « Ensemble pour une communauté en bonne santé : prévenir, dépister et agir ». Prévue du 28 août au 5 septembre 2026, cette initiative vise à renforcer la prévention des maladies à travers le dépistage précoce, la sensibilisation des populations et la promotion du don volontaire de sang. La cérémonie de lancement s’est déroulée sous le patronage du Haut-commissaire de la province de la Gnagna, Jean Baptiste Béogo représenté par le secrétaire général de la province, Mendien dit Moussa Soma, en présence du préfet, président de la délégation spéciale de la commune urbaine de Bogandé, Taugolo Paré, président de la cérémonie, du parrain de l’activité, le Dr Moussa Sawadogo, ainsi que de plusieurs autorités, responsables de services et acteurs communautaires. Dans son intervention, le représentant du Haut-commissaire, Mendien dit Moussa Soma, a salué une initiative qui traduit l’importance de la mobilisation collective dans la promotion de la santé. Il a rappelé que la prévention des maladies et la protection de la santé des populations nécessitent l’implication de tous les acteurs de la société. Camarade Soma a ainsi invité les populations à participer activement aux différentes activités prévues, notamment les séances de sensibilisation, de dépistage et de promotion du don volontaire de sang. Le préfet, président de la délégation spéciale de la commune urbaine de Bogandé, Taugolo Paré, président de la cérémonie, a, lui aussi, salué l’initiative de l’Association Baani-Mani Santé pour Tous. Selon lui, ces activités contribuent à rapprocher les actions sanitaires des populations et à renforcer les comportements favorables à la santé. Le parrain de cette première édition, le Médecin Chef du District sanitaire de Bogandé, Dr Moussa Sawadogo, a, pour sa part, insisté sur l’importance de la prévention et du dépistage précoce dans la lutte contre les maladies. Il a invité les populations, particulièrement les jeunes, les femmes et les leaders communautaires, à s’approprier pleinement cette semaine socio-sanitaire. L’un des faits marquants de la cérémonie a été la forte présence de l’Association Boalihammou des orpailleurs de la Sirba, dont des membres sont venus de plusieurs localités du Burkina Faso pour apporter leur soutien à cette initiative. Prenant la parole au nom de l’association, Yentagma Bourgou a salué la résilience des populations de la Gnagna face aux difficultés et aux nombreux défis auxquels elles sont confrontées. Il a réaffirmé la volonté de l’Association Boalihammou des orpailleurs de la Sirba de continuer à accompagner les initiatives porteuses d’espoir et susceptibles d’améliorer les conditions de vie des populations. « Nous resterons aux côtés de toute initiative salutaire qui contribue au bien-être de nos communautés », a-t-il indiqué. Le coordinateur de l’Association Baani-Mani Santé pour Tous, Alassane Dori dit Sisco, s’est réjoui de la forte mobilisation enregistrée à l’occasion de cette cérémonie. Il a exprimé sa reconnaissance aux autorités administratives, aux services de santé, aux partenaires, aux bénévoles et aux différentes bonnes volontés qui accompagnent cette initiative. Selon le camarade Dori, l’ambition de son association est de contribuer à bâtir une communauté mieux informée, davantage engagée dans la prévention et plus solidaire face aux défis sanitaires. Durant cette semaine, les populations bénéficieront de séances de sensibilisation sur différentes problématiques de santé publique, d’activités de dépistage et d’actions de promotion du don volontaire de sang. Plus de 70 poches de sang ont été collectées lors de la cérémonie d'ouverture. À travers cette première édition, l’Association Baani-Mani Santé pour Tous entend faire de la prévention, du dépistage et de la solidarité communautaire des leviers essentiels pour l’amélioration durable de la santé des populations de la Gnagna. Agence d’Information du Burkina AYT/ata/zs

items.title: Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings pledges decisive action on climate change, galamsey and environmental degradation
items.description: The newly appointed Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Rawlings, has pledged to pursue decisive action against climate change, environmental degradation, illegal mining, pollution and other challenges confronting Ghana’s environment. In a statement following her appointment, Dr Rawlings expressed gratitude to President John Dramani Mahama for the confidence reposed in her and pledged to approach the role with integrity, humility and a strong sense of responsibility. “I do not take this responsibility lightly. Public service is, first and foremost, a call to duty, sacrifice and stewardship,” she said. The Klottey Korle legislator said science, technology and innovation must play a central role in Ghana’s development, stressing the need for research to move beyond academia into practical partnerships involving government, the private sector, civil society, communities and universities. She said such collaboration should focus on creating jobs, strengthening industries, improving agriculture and healthcare, and building a more innovative and competitive economy. “The challenges before us are significant. Managing climate change, environmental degradation, illegal mining, waste management, pollution and the sustainable use of our natural resources require courage, innovation, collaboration and above all, decisive action,” she stated. The Minister said Ghana’s environment should not be viewed merely as a resource to be exploited but as an inheritance that must be protected for present and future generations. “I see our environment not as a resource to exploit, but as an inheritance entrusted to our care,” she said, pledging to protect the country’s flora and fauna, water bodies, land, air and other natural resources. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings MP (@zanetorofficial) Dr Rawlings also underscored the importance of engaging scientists, researchers, innovators, environmentalists, businesses, institutions and communities in addressing the country’s environmental and development challenges. She said she would listen, learn and engage stakeholders while working to responsibly unlock Ghana’s natural and scientific potential. “We are stewards with a duty to protect our flora and fauna, water bodies, land, air and natural resources, holding them in trust for this generation and for posterity,” she said. Dr Rawlings called on Ghanaians to support her with prayers, ideas and partnerships as she assumes responsibility for the ministry. “This is bigger than any one individual. It is about the Ghana we leave behind, and I am ready to serve,” she said. Her appointment places her at the helm of a ministry expected to play a key role in addressing some of Ghana’s most pressing environmental concerns, including illegal mining, climate change, pollution, waste management and the sustainable management of natural resources.

items.title: Bawumia was brainchild behind Domestic Gold Purchase Programme – Samuel Jinapor
items.description: Former Lands and Natural Resources Minister Samuel Abdulai Jinapor has rejected claims that seek to downplay the role of former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia in the introduction of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. Mr Jinapor, who is also the Member of Parliament for Damongo, said the programme was conceived by Dr Bawumia at a time Ghana was facing severe economic difficulties arising from the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war. In a Facebook post on Monday, August 31, 2026, he said Dr Bawumia, then Head of the Economic Management Team, held strategic meetings with relevant stakeholders before directing the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources to engage stakeholders ahead of the programme’s formal launch on June 17, 2021. According to Mr Jinapor, the programme represented a major departure from Ghana’s previous approach to accumulating gold reserves. He explained that while the country had purchased gold from abroad when it sought to increase its reserves in 1960, the new programme allowed the Bank of Ghana to purchase gold locally from licensed aggregators and mining companies, paying them the Ghana cedi equivalent of the prevailing market price. He said the programme had also significantly increased Ghana’s gold reserves, which stood at 8.77 tonnes when it was launched. “Even though the Bank of Ghana’s target was to double this figure in five (5) years, as at December 2024, less than four (4) years into the implementation of this consequential Programme, the Bank of Ghana had almost quadrupled their reserves, from 8.77 tonnes to 30.53 tonnes,” he said. Mr Jinapor further argued that the programme had contributed significantly to Ghana’s economic stability and external reserves. Quoting current Bank of Ghana Governor Dr Johnson Asiama, he said the programme had “strengthened external buffers and macroeconomic stability” and had been “crucial to the stabilisation goal of the Bank of Ghana.” He therefore urged the public record to reflect that the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme was the brainchild of Dr Bawumia.

items.title: Fuel prices set to go up from September 1, Petrol to sell at GHC 16.69 and Diesel, GHC 17.90 – COMAC
items.description: The Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies has released its Outlook Report on the expected price movements for the various petroleum products from September 1 to 16, 2026. The data showed that petrol will go up by as much as 4.80%, with a litre likely to be sold at GHC 16.39. Diesel should witness a 2.10% spike, with a litre going for GHC 17.60 per litre. LPG, on the other hand, will go down by 0.93%, resulting in a kilogramme selling at GHC 13.73. Reasons According to the Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies, COMAC, the increase has been influenced by rising crude oil prices on the international market and higher prices of finished petroleum products. It stated that international crude oil prices rose by 1.75%, as all refined petroleum products recorded increases. Petrol posted the highest rise at 8.86%, followed by diesel at 5.51% and LPG at 3.31%. Average crude oil prices rose by 1.75%, from US$90.53/bbl to US$92.11/bbl, despite the United States announcing its toughest sanctions against Iran. The sanctions had limited immediate impact, as unsuccessful mediation by Qatar and Pakistan and uncertainty over Strait of Hormuz transits kept prices elevated. All refined petroleum products increased, led by petrol at 8.86%, diesel at 5.51% and LPG at 3.31%. The cedi appreciated by 3.64% to GH¢11.3697/US$ based on average bank rates between 12 and 27 August 2026. This reversed three consecutive pricing windows of depreciation and marked its strongest level since June 2026. The higher projected adjustments reflect rising global crude oil and refined product prices despite the cedi’s appreciation. However, the government industry intervention will continue to moderate diesel price increases. There are currently more than 200 oil marketing companies in the country, and there are strong indications that some of them will move quickly to adjust prices from 6 a.m. on September 1, 2026, while others may try to monitor competition before they review their prices at the pumps. Government Subsidy Based on our checks, the price of diesel would have been higher than what the Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies had projected for diesel. It is for this reason that a litre of diesel is likely to sell at GHC 17.60. A highly placed government source today revealed to JOY BUSINESS that the government has taken the decision to extend its GH¢2 per litre reduction in the regulatory margin on diesel into the first pricing window of September, in a move aimed at cushioning consumers against rising fuel prices. Government sources maintained that the intervention followed concerns over a possible increase in diesel prices at the pumps in the coming pricing window. The reduction, which was introduced as a temporary measure covering two pricing windows, was originally expected to expire at the end of August. Price Floor The National Petroleum Authority has increased the price floor for the various petroleum products from September 1 to 16, 2026. Petrol will be sold at GH¢14.53, and diesel will be pegged at GH¢15.60. This should mean that no oil marketing company should sell below these quotes from tomorrow, September 1, 2026. This represents about a 4.38% increase with respect to the benchmark. Diesel has also gone up from GH¢15.19 to GH¢15.60, representing a 2.69% increase. LPG, however, has been reduced from GH¢10.98 to GH¢10.85 per kilogramme.

items.title: Gnagna/Manni : La Délégation spéciale autorise la signature de deux conventions et l’ouverture de concours professionnels
items.description: BURKINA-SIRBA-GNAGNA-MANNI-DELEGATION-SPECIALE-SESSION-EXTRAORDINAIRE Gnagna/Manni : La Délégation spéciale autorise la signature de deux conventions et l'ouverture de concours professionnels Manni, 27 août 2026 (AIB) – La Délégation spéciale (DS) de la commune de Manni a tenu, jeudi 27 août 2026, sa première session extraordinaire de l'année. Présidée par Emmanuel Tindano, Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS), cette rencontre a permis aux membres statutaires d'adopter des délibérations autorisant la signature de conventions avec l'Agence d'Information du Burkina (AIB) et l'Agence nationale d'appui au développement des collectivités territoriales (ADCT), ainsi que l'ouverture de concours professionnels au profit du personnel communal. À l'ouverture des travaux, le Préfet, Président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Manni, Emmanuel Tindano a présenté l'ordre du jour et invité les membres à une participation dynamique aux échanges, en vue d'un examen attentif des dossiers soumis à leur appréciation. Cinq points étaient inscrits à l'ordre du jour : la lecture et l'approbation du procès-verbal de la session précédente ; l'examen des délibérations autorisant la signature des conventions avec l'AIB et l'ADCT ; l'autorisation d'ouverture de concours professionnels au profit du personnel de la mairie ainsi que les informations et divers. À l'issue des échanges, les membres de la Délégation spéciale ont adopté à l'unanimité les trois délibérations soumises à leur examen par acclamations. La délibération autorisant la signature de la convention avec l'ADCT s'inscrit, elle, dans la dynamique d'accompagnement des collectivités territoriales et de renforcement de leurs capacités. La délibération portant ouverture de concours professionnels, pour le recrutement d'un adjoint administratif, d'un assistant des services financiers et d'un administrateur civil, a été saluée par le technicien communal, Dieudonné Tindano, qui y voit une avancée significative pour la carrière des agents municipaux et une opportunité d'évolution professionnelle pour le personnel concerné. Au titre des divers, le Médecin chef du District sanitaire de Manni, Dr Traoré Lacina, a annoncé la reprise des travaux de finition du Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) de Manni, une information saluée par les conseillers. S'exprimant au nom du secteur de l'éducation, Madiéga Daporé a remercié la Délégation spéciale pour son accompagnement constant, tout en s'inquiétant du devenir de l'inspection, dont le bâtiment est fortement dégradé. Il a été rassuré par le responsable des marchés publics qui a annoncé deux nouvelles : l'avancée du processus en vue de l'octroi d'un bâtiment mieux adapté et l'acquisition de moyens d'éclairage au profit du service social. Le responsable de l'Action sociale a fait part de l'installation des Comités communautaires mixtes (CCM) dans les secteurs, des cadres de concertation destinés à renforcer le dialogue autour des questions de développement local. Il a salué l'acquisition annoncée de moyens d'éclairage, qui devrait contribuer à résorber le déficit d'énergie électrique affectant le bâtiment du service social. La Journée communale de résilience et du mérite des travailleurs du public comme du privé a par ailleurs été évoquée par le PDS, Emmanuel Tindano, qui a insisté sur l'importance de féliciter et de remercier l'ensemble des acteurs publics et privés pour leur engagement au service de la commune. Dans son mot de clôture, le PDS a salué la participation des membres, et s'est réjoui de la qualité des échanges. Par ailleurs, il a invité chacun à poursuivre les efforts engagés pour le bon fonctionnement de la commune. Agence d'Information du Burkina GL/ayt/ata/zs

items.title: Our World Our People withdrawn due to curriculum duplication, not politics – Adutwum’s spokesperson
items.description: The spokesperson for former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has rejected claims that the withdrawal of Our World Our People from Ghana’s primary school curriculum was politically motivated. Eric Yaw Opoku Mensah said it is “factually inaccurate” to suggest that the subject was removed because it projected the ideology or interests of a particular political party. His comments follow remarks by Enoch Gyetuah, a member of the Board of Directors of the National Schools and Inspectorate Authority, who reportedly suggested in an interview on Adom FM that the subject was withdrawn for political reasons. Mr Mensah said, “the decision was instead based on a curriculum review that identified significant duplication and redundancy in the content of Our World Our People, particularly in relation to Religious and Moral Education (RME).” According to him, several sub-strands and focal areas contained considerable similarities, making it unnecessarily repetitive to continue teaching the content as a separate subject. He said the decision followed curriculum analysis, assessment of knowledge overlap and feedback from teachers and other stakeholders. Mr Mensah stressed that the withdrawal was therefore not an attempt to prevent the projection of the interests or ideology of any political party. He also challenged claims that the smooth implementation of the basic school curriculum had been hampered by a lack of textbooks. According to him, records from the Ministry of Education and the Ghana Education Service procurement units indicate that 13,922,851 textbooks had been supplied through regional and district education offices to schools. He urged stakeholders to verify such claims with the relevant institutions before putting them into the public domain. “Education policy must be debated based on evidence, professional judgment, and the best interests of learners and not misinformation or political convenience,” Mr Mensah said. He further called on individuals holding positions of authority within the education sector to exercise greater caution when commenting on policy decisions, stressing that inaccurate information could undermine public confidence in the education system. Mr Mensah said the facts surrounding the withdrawal of Our World Our People are contained in a letter from the Ghana Education Service communicating the decision to remove the subject from the primary school curriculum. He maintained that the focus of education policy discussions should be on improving learning outcomes and ensuring that curriculum decisions serve the best interests of Ghanaian pupils.

items.title: Lionel Messi range définitivement le maillot de l’Albiceleste
items.description: Après plus de deux décennies sous le maillot de l’Argentine, Lionel Messi a annoncé, ce lundi 31 août 2026, sa retraite internationale. À 39 ans, l’octuple Ballon d’Or quitte l’Albiceleste avec un palmarès exceptionnel, marqué notamment par un sacre mondial en 2022 et deux Copa América. C’est une page majeure de l’histoire du football argentin qui se tourne. Lionel Messi a annoncé, ce lundi 31 août 2026, sur son compte Instagram, qu’il mettait un terme à sa carrière internationale. Le capitaine emblématique de l’Albiceleste quitte ainsi la sélection après 207 apparitions et 125 buts, selon plusieurs sources médiatiques. Champion du monde en 2022, double vainqueur de la Copa América et recordman des sélections argentines, Messi referme un chapitre long de plus de vingt ans avec son pays. Une décision qu’il dit avoir mûrement réfléchie, notamment après la finale du dernier Mondial, perdue par l’Argentine face à l’Espagne (1-0 après prolongation), mais aussi dans le contexte douloureux du décès de son père et agent, Jorge Messi. «Après tout ce temps qui s'est écoulé depuis la finale, après y avoir beaucoup réfléchi, je veux vous annoncer à tous que je prends ma retraite de la sélection… C'est une décision qui m'a fait et qui me fait encore mal au fond de l'âme, mais je comprends que c'est le moment», a écrit l’octuple Ballon d’Or, selon plusieurs médias. Dans son message, le joueur assure avoir «toujours tout donné» pour le maillot national et dit quitter la sélection avec «la tranquillité d'esprit et la fierté» d’avoir, avec ses coéquipiers, offert à l’Argentine «des moments dont nous avons rêvé». «Je n'ai plus rien à donner» Conscient que la fin de son aventure internationale approche, Lionel Messi évoque également la relève qui se profile au sein de la sélection argentine. «Il ne me reste plus beaucoup de temps, les étapes se succèdent et celle-ci me fait particulièrement mal. J'aime, j'ai aimé et j'aimerai toujours la sélection. J'ai tout donné, je n'ai plus rien à donner, il y a de très bons jeunes qui arrivent derrière et qui méritent leur place», a-t-il poursuivi. Messi révèle, par ailleurs, avoir rédigé son message dès le 21 juillet, soit deux jours après la finale du Mondial. Le décès de son père aurait ensuite renforcé sa conviction de tourner définitivement la page de la sélection. «Aujourd'hui, après ce qui est arrivé à mon père, j'en suis encore plus convaincu qu'avant», affirme-t-il. Pour sa dernière compétition internationale, la légende argentine aura une nouvelle fois marqué les esprits. Messi a inscrit huit buts, dont un triplé, et porté l’Albiceleste jusqu’en finale. Mais l’ultime rendez-vous s’est conclu par une défaite face à l’Espagne, au terme des prolongations. À 39 ans, l’octuple Ballon d’Or évolue toujours en club sous les couleurs de l’Inter Miami, aux États-Unis. Ce n’est pas la première fois que Messi annonce son retrait de la sélection. En 2016, après une nouvelle désillusion, il avait déjà annoncé une première retraite internationale, avant de revenir quelques mois plus tard et de poursuivre son aventure avec l’Argentine jusqu’au sacre mondial au Qatar en 2022. Avec cette nouvelle annonce, Lionel Messi s’apprête donc à refermer définitivement son histoire avec l’Albiceleste, après avoir marqué de son empreinte plusieurs générations de supporters argentins et écrit l’une des plus belles pages du football mondial. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Lionel Messi range définitivement le maillot de l’Albiceleste est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
